answer: Two measurements must agree at each dark-sky apiary seat. A seat is one named hive yard in a reserve; each epoch the keeper files refractometer readings for nectar from three combs and an all-sky frame. Dew and bloom timing make sugar readings unprecomputable, while the star field fixes place and hour: a clear night must show the comet's tail or the nebula's glow. A hundred sybil identities need a hundred colonies, permits and a keeper visiting each yard, so outlay scales linearly while per-seat payoff stays flat. One camera's fixed-pattern noise betrays reuse, and both bonds are slashed.
